caption: Seven habits, and where Ordinance DS stands on each

columns.label: Why it matters in an audit

rows.habit: Keep every secret in a secrets manager from the first day.
rows.why: A key in a file or in a chat has no owner, no log and no end date.

rows.habit: Treat every value that is built into browser code as public.
rows.why: Every reader of the page can read it, whatever the variable is called.

rows.habit: Use the strict security policy from the first commit.
rows.why: Inline code that is found late forces a rewrite just before the audit.

rows.habit: Keep every file from others pinned, listed and on your own server.
rows.why: A file that loads from another server at run time is in no bill of materials.

rows.habit: Remove personal data before a log or a measurement leaves your system.
rows.why: A user id or an address in a tool of another company is a transfer of personal data.

rows.habit: Pin every step of the pipeline, and run no install script.
rows.why: A step that follows a moving tag runs code that nobody reviewed, with your keys.

rows.habit: Judge every tool with the six questions, also a well-known one.
rows.why: A sound tool that is used in an unsound way still gives a finding.
